questions.answer: Its better to live off campus if you study at UoC or the hospital. Find an accommodation within the walls of Heraklion or close to Chranioporta where you easily can get the bus to the University.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Some many good outdoor opportunities, go hike Psiloritis and Gingilos. Go to Prevelli beach, Balos beach, Richtis Gorge, Archanes city. With student discount on the ferry tickets its cheap to go to Santorini and Athens.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Depends on the person. Everything in Greece is late back and not as punctual as in Denmark. I liked it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Greeks are very open, just go and talk with them. They might not always approach you, but if you go and talk with them they are always interested in talking

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The greek culture was easy to enjoy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: openness, laidback attitude

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't expect to learn as much academically as you would do in Denmark. The language barrier makes it difficult for optimal learning when you are doing a clinical rotation. You do the exchange because of the overall experience and you learn a lot of other useful stuff. Definitely worth it and still a great learning experience.  
2. Dont stress about not having everything figured out before arriving, accommodation, transportation etc. etc.. Everything is easier once you have arrived, I know many people who arrived with no accommodation and found it quickly once they arrived. 
3. Find a place to live near the center/chanioporta. All the social stuff happens within the walls.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want a student card, get a greek phone number.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many nice people from all over Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Always having to approach and get to know some many new people in a short periode of time.
